Do I need Making Tax Digital, and when?

If you're a sole trader or landlord and your self-employment plus property income before expenses is over £50,000, you should already be using it. Over £30,000, April 2027. Over £20,000, April 2028.

See matching software Compare all 179 products

Every fact on this page comes from GOV.UK and is linked. Last checked 18 November 2026. How we check.

Who needs to use it

According to HMRC, you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax if all of these apply:

  • you're a sole trader or a landlord registered for Self Assessment
  • you get income from self-employment or property, or both
  • your qualifying income is over the threshold for the relevant tax year

Source: GOV.UK, Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.

When you need to start

If your qualifying income was over……in the tax yearYou need to use MTD from
£50,0002024 to 20256 April 2026 (now live)
£30,0002025 to 20266 April 2027
£20,0002026 to 20276 April 2028

HMRC checks your Self Assessment tax return each year. If you're over the threshold it will write to you, but HMRC is clear that if you don't get a letter it is still your responsibility to check. Partnerships will need to join later; HMRC hasn't set the date yet.

Starting in April 2027? See how and when to sign up if you're over £30,000, including whether HMRC signs you up and the key dates for your first year.

Source: GOV.UK. You can also use HMRC's own checker tool.

What counts as qualifying income

Qualifying income is your total income from self-employment and property, before expenses (your turnover), based on the tax return for the earlier tax year. HMRC's own example: £25,000 of rental income plus £27,000 of self-employment income gives qualifying income of £52,000.

It does not include employment (PAYE) income, your share of profit from a partnership as an individual partner, dividends (including from your own company), the State Pension or private pensions.

Source: GOV.UK, Work out your qualifying income.

What you'll have to do

  1. Keep digital records of your self-employment and property income and expenses in compatible software.
  2. Send quarterly updates every 3 months. These are summaries, not tax returns. Each one covers the tax year so far.
  3. Submit your tax return through software by 31 January after the tax year, adding any other income.

Source: GOV.UK, Choose the right software.

Quarterly update deadlines

Standard period (tax year)Calendar periodDeadline
6 April to 5 July1 April to 30 June7 August
6 April to 5 October1 April to 30 September7 November
6 April to 5 January1 April to 31 December7 February
6 April to 5 April1 April to 31 March7 May (following tax year)

If you've had no income or expenses in a period, you still have to send the update. If you want calendar periods, choose that in your software before you send your first update, because you can't change it for the rest of the tax year afterwards.

Source: GOV.UK, Send quarterly updates.

Penalties

Late quarterly updates earn penalty points, and reaching the points threshold means a £200 penalty. For the 2026 to 2027 tax year, HMRC will not apply penalty points for late quarterly updates, but you must send them before you can submit your tax return, and late tax returns still get points.

Source: GOV.UK, Send quarterly updates.

If you own property jointly

For jointly let property, HMRC lets you include either income and expenses, or income only, in your quarterly updates. If you leave out expenses, you report them after the tax year by resending your fourth quarterly update before you submit your tax return. Properties you own alone still need both income and expenses in every update.

Source: GOV.UK, Send quarterly updates. See which software confirms joint-property support with the joint property filter, or read our full guide to jointly owned property under MTD.

Who is exempt

  • Qualifying income of £20,000 or less: automatically exempt.
  • No National Insurance number before the start of the tax year: automatically exempt.
  • Partnerships: don't currently need to use it.
  • Some people, for example those who are digitally excluded, can apply for an exemption.

If you're exempt you still send a Self Assessment tax return as normal.

Source: GOV.UK, Find out if you can get an exemption.

Quick answers

Do I need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax?

You need to use it if you're a sole trader or landlord registered for Self Assessment, you get income from self-employment or property (or both), and your qualifying income is over the threshold for the relevant tax year.

What are the Making Tax Digital thresholds?

Over £50,000 of qualifying income in the 2024 to 2025 tax year means you start from 6 April 2026. Over £30,000 in 2025 to 2026 means from 6 April 2027. Over £20,000 in 2026 to 2027 means from 6 April 2028.

Does my salary count towards the MTD threshold?

No. Qualifying income is your self-employment and property income before expenses. Employment (PAYE) income, a share of partnership profit, dividends and pensions do not count.

What if my qualifying income is £20,000 or less?

HMRC says you are automatically exempt and do not need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax. You still send a Self Assessment tax return as normal.

Will I get a penalty for a late quarterly update in 2026 to 2027?

HMRC says it will not apply penalty points for late quarterly updates during the 2026 to 2027 tax year. You still need to send them before you can submit your tax return, and late tax returns still get penalty points.
